name: chordii
desc: Text file to music sheet converter
why: Converts plain text chord sheets into music sheets, a small text-to-notation transform with an old-school feel.

brief.what_it_is: Chordii is a command-line utility for printing song lyrics with chords. Per the Homepage's header line, it was formerly known as CHORD. The homepage gives no details on input or output formats, though the Homebrew description calls it a text file to music sheet converter, and the brew executables are a2crd and chordii. The homepage does not describe the mechanism or show any usage.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames Chordii as a tool for printing lyrics with chords, and says it has been discontinued in favour of its successor, ChordPro.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no installation instructions. The brew executables listed (a2crd and chordii) come from the package metadata, not from the homepage, and no commands were seen on the page.
brief.standout: The page is a closing notice rather than a project pitch: the author says Chordii has been discontinued and points readers to ChordPro, described as a newly developed but still mostly compatible successor.
brief.status: Discontinued. The homepage states 'Chordii has been discontinued.' Copyright runs 2007-2021 and the page was last modified 09-Aug-2021. No release or commit information was checked.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a discontinuation notice, so the project is no longer developed. It names a 'ChordPro site' without giving a URL, so the successor link could not be followed from this page. The README and docs were not available, so features and input syntax are unverified. The copyright notice is 'All Rights Reserved', which the brief should note as a licensing concern.
quotes: Its successor is a newly developed yet still mostly compatible tool ChordPro that can be found on the ChordPro site.
fetch_log: https://www.vromans.org/johan/projects/Chordii/ - fetched successfully; discontinuation notice only, no README, docs, or demo; the ChordPro successor is named but no URL is given, so it was not followed
